title: Calculate Cumulative Academic Credits Earned Per Student

title: Filter Employees Earning Strictly Above Their Department Average

title: Filter Orders Once Customer Cumulative Spend Crosses 200

title: Analyze Cumulative Department Payroll Progression Against Total Budget

starter_query:
-- Cumulative department payroll against total budget
SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.dept_id, e.salary,

solution_query: SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.dept_id, e.salary, SUM(e.salary) OVER (PARTITION BY e.dept_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC, e.emp_id ASC) AS running_dept_salary, d.budget, ROUND((SUM(e.salary) OVER (PARTITION BY e.dept_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC, e.emp_id ASC) / d.budget) * 100, 2) AS pct_budget_spent FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id ORDER BY e.dept_id ASC, e.salary DESC, e.emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Joining the department budget and comparing it to the cumulative salary burn reveals at what salary tier the departmental budget is exhausted.
common_mistakes: Dividing running salary by employee salary instead of department budget.
interview_tip: Correlating running spend to static budget ceilings is a cornerstone of corporate financial planning and FP&A models.
